prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Pleasanton California?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t say there is one universally “best” personal injury lawyer in Pleasanton — the right lawyer depends on your type of injury, the facts of your case, and which attorney’s experience and working style fit you. I can, however, help you find the best lawyer for your situation and give you a short list of practical steps.

Quick steps to find a top Pleasanton personal injury lawyer
1. Search reputable directories and peer-review lists:
   - Super Lawyers (Northern California listings)
   - Martindale-Hubbell (peer-review ratings)
   - Avvo (ratings + client reviews)
   - California State Bar (verify license and discipline history)
2. Check local sources:
   - Google and Yelp reviews
   - Alameda County/Contra Costa County court records for verdicts/settlements
   - Local referrals (friends, doctors, other attorneys)
3. Look for relevant experience:
   - Substantial experience handling the specific type of case you have (auto, bicycle, premises, workplace, wrongful death, etc.)
   - Trial experience and courtroom presence (many cases settle, but trial-ready attorneys often get better settlements)
   - Track record of significant settlements/verdicts in similar cases
4. Confirm fee structure and costs:
   - Most personal injury lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you win). Typical contingency: roughly 33%–40%, depending on whether the case settles or goes to trial. Ask for details in writing.
5. Verify communication and availability:
   - Do they return calls, explain strategy clearly, and keep you updated?
   - Will a senior attorney handle your case or mostly paralegals?

Questions to ask during a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine before? How many and with what results?
- What is your assessment of my claim and likely value/range?
- Who will work on my case day-to-day? Who will I talk to?
- What is your fee and how are out-of-pocket costs handled?
- Do you try cases? If so, how often do you go to trial?
- Can you provide references from former clients?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific result
- Poor or no online presence and no clear disciplinary history or references
- High-pressure tactics to sign immediately
- Unclear fee or cost arrangements

If you want, I can:
- Suggest a short list of Pleasanton-area firms based on typical reputation sources (I can’t browse the web right now, but I can show how to search or format search queries you can use).
- Draft a phone/email script you can use to contact attorneys.
- Help you evaluate responses from three attorneys you interview.

Which would you prefer: a short list of local firms (I can give search terms and places to check), a ready-to-use consultation script, or help evaluating attorney responses? Also tell me the type of injury/accident — that will let me tailor recommendations.
